Battle''' (born May 10, 2001) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Toronto Raptors]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[George Washington Colonials men's basketball|George Washington Colonials]] of the [[Atlantic 10 Conference]], and the [[Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball|Minnesota Golden Gophers]] and [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State Buckeyes]] of the [[Big Ten Conference]]. ==High school career== Battle played basketball for [[DeLaSalle High School (Minneapolis)|DeLaSalle High School]] in [[Minneapolis|Minneapolis, Minnesota]], where he was teammates with [[Tyrell Terry]].{{cite web|first=Mike|last=Max|title=Tyrell Terry & Jamison Battle, DeLaSalle's Dynamic Duo, Aim For 1 Last State Title|url=https://minnesota.cbslocal.com/2019/02/15/tyrell-terry-jamison-battle-delasalles-dynamic-duo-aim-for-1-last-state-title/|website=CBSLocal.com|publisher=[[WCCO-TV]]|date=February 15, 2019|access-date=December 17, 2021}} As a senior, he averaged 21.2 points and nine rebounds per game, helping his team win the Class 3A state title.{{cite web|title=Battle Brings Scoring Ability to Gophers|url=https://gophersports.com/news/2021/4/27/mens-basketball-battle-brings-scoring-ability-to-gophers.aspx|website=GopherSports.com|publisher=University of Minnesota Athletics|date=April 27, 2021|access-date=December 17, 2021}} ==College career== As a freshman at [[George Washington Colonials men's basketball|George Washington]], Battle averaged 11.8 points and 5.2 rebounds per game, and was named to the [[Atlantic 10 Conference|Atlantic 10]] All-Rookie Team.{{cite web|first=Eric|last=Detweiler|title=Ready For Their Shot|url=https://gwsports.com/news/2020/11/17/mens-basketball-ready-for-their-shot|website=GWSports.com|publisher=George Washington University Athletics|date=November 19, 2020|access-date=December 17, 2021}} He set a program single-season record with 89 three-pointers, which also led the conference.{{cite web|first=Emily|last=Maise|title=Pair of sophomore forwards to transfer from men's basketball program|url=https://www.gwhatchet.com/2021/03/08/pair-of-sophomore-forwards-to-transfer-from-mens-basketball-program/|work=[[The GW Hatchet]]|date=March 8, 2021|access-date=December 17, 2021}} On January 3, 2021, Battle posted a career-high 29 points and seven rebounds in a 75–73 win against [[Duquesne Dukes men's basketball|Duquesne]].{{cite web|title=Battle carries George Washington past Duquesne 75-73|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401274402|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=January 3, 2021|access-date=December 17, 2021}} As a sophomore, he averaged 17.3 points and 5.2 rebounds per game, earning Third Team All-Atlantic 10 honors.{{cite web|first=Travis|last=Branham|title=George Washington sophomore Jamison Battle enters Transfer Portal|url=https://247sports.com/college/basketball/recruiting/Article/Jamison-Battle-transfer-George-Washington-basketball-162055764/|work=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]]|date=March 8, 2021|access-date=December 17, 2021}} For his junior season, Battle transferred to [[Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball|Minnesota]] to play under first-year head coach [[Ben Johnson (basketball)|Ben Johnson]].{{cite web|first=Marcus|last=Fuller|title=Gophers' Jamison Battle proving to be among Big Ten's top scorers but wants to be the 'total package'|url=https://www.startribune.com/gophers-jamison-battle-proving-to-be-among-big-tens-top-scorers-but-wants-to-be-the-total-package/600120486/|work=[[Star Tribune]]|date=November 24, 2021|access-date=December 17, 2021}} He was named Honorable Mention All-[[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]].{{cite press release|title=2021-22 Big Ten Men's Basketball Postseason Honors Announced|url=https://bigten.org/news/2022/3/8/2021-22-big-ten-mens-basketball-postseason-honors-announced.aspx|website=BigTen.org|publisher=[[Big Ten Conference]]|date=March 8, 2022|access-date=March 8, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220308180525/https://bigten.org/news/2022/3/8/2021-22-big-ten-mens-basketball-postseason-honors-announced.aspx|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 8, 2022}} Battle averaged 17.5 points and 6.3 rebounds per game as a junior. As a senior, he averaged 12.4 points per game. Battle transferred to [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]] for his final collegiate season.{{cite news |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |title=Jamison Battle announces he will transfer to Ohio State |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/36093120/jamison-battle-announces-transfer-ohio-state |access-date=November 26, 2024 |date=April 6, 2023}} Battle passed the 2,000 career point mark in his final game, a loss to [[Georgia Bulldogs basketball|Georgia]] in the [[2024 National Invitation Tournament]].{{cite web|title=Buckeyes Fall Just Short in 79-77 Loss to Georgia|url=https://ohiostatebuckeyes.com/news/2024/3/27/mens-basketball-buckeyes-fall-just-short-in-79-77-loss-to-georgia|website=OhioStateBuckeyes.com|publisher=[[Ohio State Buckeyes]]|date=March 27, 2024|access-date=March 31, 2024|quote=Battle finishes his final season scoring 20 or more points in four of his last five games. He also went over 2,000 career points on Tuesday.}} ==Professional career== === Toronto Raptors/Raptors 905 (2024–present)=== After going undrafted in the [[2024 NBA draft]], Battle signed with the [[Toronto Raptors]] on July 16, 2024,{{cite web|title=RAPTORS SIGN BATTLE|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-sign-battle|website=NBA.com|date=July 16, 2024|access-date=July 19, 2024}}{{cite web|first=Sam|last=Amico|title=Raptors Signing Ohio State's Jamison Battle For Summer League|url=https://www.yardbarker.com/college_basketball/articles/amp/raptors_signing_ohio_states_jamison_battle_for_summer_league/s1_17038_40541884|website=YardBarker.com|date=June 27, 2024|access-date=June 29, 2024}} and on October 19 Toronto converted his deal into a [[two-way contract]].{{cite web|title=RAPTORS WAIVE THREE, CONVERT BATTLE TO TWO-WAY CONTRACT|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-waive-three-convert-battle-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=October 19, 2024|access-date=October 19, 2024}} On November 27, Battle scored a career-high 24 points on 9-of-11 shooting, including 6-of-8 three-pointers, in a 119-93 road win against the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].{{cite web|last=Grange|first=Michael|title=Raptors Takeaways: Contributions from entire lineup lead to first road win|url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nba/article/raptors-takeaways-contributions-from-entire-lineup-lead-to-first-road-win/|website=sportsnet.ca|date=November 28, 2024}} Battle's contract was converted into a standard, three-year contract on February 7, 2025.{{Cite web |date=February 7, 2025 |title=Raptors Sign Rookie Sharpshooter to Multi-Year Deal |url=https://www.si.com/nba/raptors/toronto-raptors-sign-jamison-battle-to-multi-year-deal |access-date=February 7, 2025 |website=Toronto Raptors On SI |language=en-US}}{{Cite web|title=Ex-Gophers star Jamison Battle lands three-year contract with Raptors|url=https://www.si.com/college/minnesota/gophers-basketball/ex-gophers-star-jamison-battle-lands-three-year-contract-with-raptors-01jkgzk6ncz6|access-date=February 11, 2025|website=si.com|language=en}} On April 23, 2026, Battle scored 14 points in 16 minutes off the bench, contributing to the Raptors' 126-104 victory during Game 3 of the first round playoff series against [[Cleveland Cavaliers]]. All of the points were scored in the fourth quarter, helping to fuel an offensive run that secured the win and bring the series to 2-1. Battle's performance included a perfect shooting night, as he made all of his field goal attempts.{{Cite web |title=How Raptors’ Battle ‘flipped script’ on Cavaliers in massive Game 3 |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nba/video/how-raptors-battle-flipped-script-on-cavaliers-in-massive-game-3/ |access-date=2026-04-25 |website=www.sportsnet.ca}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player
